_note: Golden expectations for the `check` (Stage 4) compliance judge — ID-FREE. We do NOT reference rule IDs: those are generated by `extract` and drift when it re-runs. Instead we anchor to things that never change: the band, and verbatim PHRASES from the fixture text. This makes the eval deterministic and re-extract-proof. See README.md for scoring semantics.
_band_policy: Mirrors src/commands/check.ts: FAIL = >=1 HIGH-severity non_compliant; WARN = only medium/low non_compliant and/or >=1 needs_review; PASS = no non_compliant and no needs_review.

_fields.band: Expected PASS/WARN/FAIL (deterministic from verdict counts, no rule named).
_fields.must_catch: Verbatim offending phrases from the fixture; EACH must be quoted as `evidence` by some non_compliant verdict. Choose the core offending tokens. Matched as a normalized substring, so a judge quoting a longer fragment still counts.
_fields.expect_needs_review: Verbatim phrases; AT LEAST ONE must be quoted as `evidence` by a needs_review verdict (unverifiable external fact).
_fields.forbid_flag: Verbatim innocent phrases (risk warnings, anti-pressure wording); NONE may be quoted as `evidence` by a non_compliant verdict. False-positive guard.

01-crypto-getrich-fomo.txt.scenario: Crypto get-rich hype + FOMO + AI-bot 'money while you sleep'.
01-crypto-getrich-fomo.txt.why: Unrealistic profit promise + FOMO/urgency + no risk warning. Multiple high breaches → FAIL.

02-guaranteed-returns.txt.scenario: Investment marketed as 'guaranteed 8%', 'risk-free', '100% safe' + rate-drop urgency.
02-guaranteed-returns.txt.why: 'Guaranteed'/'risk-free'/'100% safe' for a return-bearing investment is misleading on its face — a breach, NOT needs_review (the defect is the framing, not an unverifiable fact).

03-target-vulnerable-debt.txt.scenario: Targets people in debt; 'trade your way out', 'anyone can do this'.
03-target-vulnerable-debt.txt.why: Aims a high-risk activity at vulnerable consumers and implies a reliable escape from financial trouble — vulnerability exploitation + foreseeable harm + misleading.

04-cfd-leverage.txt.scenario: CFD leverage — 'amplify your profits'; a bare 'Capital at risk' line, no loss balance.
04-cfd-leverage.txt.why: Upside emphasised while leverage's symmetric amplification of losses is unstated; a token risk line does not balance it. The risk line itself must NOT be cited as the breach (forbid_flag) — this is the 'a risk phrase is present but the ad is still unbalanced' test.

05-deposit-bonus-urgency.txt.why: Manufactured urgency + a 'free money' inducement pressures a rushed decision — behavioural-bias exploitation + foreseeable harm.

06-testimonial-profit.txt.scenario: Testimonial implying typical profit ('made £5,000 in my first month', 'quit my job').
06-testimonial-profit.txt.why: A prominent profit testimonial with no balance implies atypical results are typical — a misleading promotion. (A judge may also route it to needs_review; the misleading framing is a breach regardless, hence must_catch on the claim.)

07-awards-unverifiable.txt.scenario: Balanced ad whose ONLY concerns are externally verifiable facts: award, user count, rating.
07-awards-unverifiable.txt.why: The factual claims are compliant-if-true / misleading-if-false → needs_review, not non_compliant. Prominent risk warning present → no high breach → WARN. The risk warning must not itself be flagged. Clean needs_review case #1.

08-jargon-simple-product.txt.scenario: A simple ISA smothered in unexplained jargon.
08-jargon-simple-product.txt.why: Not misleading and risk disclosed, but unexplained jargon breaches plain-language (a medium defect) → WARN. CALIBRATION case: if the judge quotes a different jargon term (e.g. 'alpha') the substring won't match — band WARN is the primary signal here.

09-compliant-crypto.txt.scenario: High-risk product marketed responsibly: prominent loss warning, no hype, anti-pressure.
forbid_flag: lose all the money you invest
09-compliant-crypto.txt.why: A high-risk product done right must PASS. The warning phrases must not be flagged — a keyword matcher would misfire on 'high risk'/'lose all'; the judge must not.

10-compliant-isa.txt.scenario: Mainstream balanced ISA ad: costs disclosed, capital-at-risk warning, anti-pressure.
10-compliant-isa.txt.why: The 'obviously fine' baseline. Any non_compliant here is a false positive; the anti-pressure and risk phrasing must not be flagged.

11-service-maintenance.txt.scenario: Pure operational notice (scheduled maintenance). No promotion.
11-service-maintenance.txt.why: Non-promotional admin message: nothing to flag. The judge should return compliant/not_applicable across the board, not manufacture breaches from benign text.

12-support-exit-barriers.txt.scenario: 2 minutes to open, but exit only by post, 30 working days, £25 fee.
12-support-exit-barriers.txt.why: Post-only closure + 30-day delay + fee are unreasonable barriers to exit versus 2-minute onboarding — a support/good-faith breach. Exercises the support dimension.

13-pro-product-to-retail.txt.scenario: An institutional-grade leveraged product pushed to 'everyone' with 'no eligibility checks'.
13-pro-product-to-retail.txt.why: A product 'reserved for institutional desks' is offered to retail with no eligibility gating — professional-only scope leakage, plus unexplained complex leverage. Exercises the financial-promotion-scope dimension.

14-remediation-notice.txt.scenario: A redress notice done well: prompt, apologetic, clear, automatic refund, no spin.
14-remediation-notice.txt.why: A remedial/harm notice that is clear, fair and not misleading — compliant. Tests that a non-promotional but obligation-bearing message is not misread as a breach.

15-comparative-lowest-fees.txt.scenario: Balanced ad whose issue is a comparative superlative: 'lowest fees of any UK broker'.
expect_needs_review: lowest fees of any UK broker
15-comparative-lowest-fees.txt.why: A market-wide comparative price claim: compliant if substantiated, misleading if not → needs_review. Risk warning present → WARN. Clean needs_review case #2.

16-fscs-protection-claim.txt.scenario: Implies capital/loss protection: 'your money is fully protected' for a market-risk investment.
16-fscs-protection-claim.txt.why: 'Fully protected'/'safe' misrepresents investment risk — FSCS-type schemes do not cover market losses. Materially misleading safety claim causing foreseeable harm.

17-advice-recommendation.txt.scenario: Firm issues a mass 'buy now' recommendation with urgency.
17-advice-recommendation.txt.why: A blanket recommendation to all readers with manufactured urgency ('the perfect time', 'before everyone else') — FOMO exploitation + misleading/unbalanced (implies suitability for everyone, no risk).

18-disclaimer-overload.txt.scenario: A one-line CTA buried under a wall of ~14 stacked disclaimers.
18-disclaimer-overload.txt.why: The disclaimer wall obscures rather than informs — a presentation defect (unnecessary disclaimers / overload), medium at most → WARN. Aggregate breach with no single offending phrase, so the WARN band is the assertion (CALIBRATION case).

19-mostly-ok-one-breach.txt.scenario: A compliant ISA ad with ONE blatant guarantee bolted on.
must_catch: double your money in year one, guaranteed
19-mostly-ok-one-breach.txt.why: Discrimination + evidence-localization test: most of the text is fine, so the judge must isolate and quote the single offending clause verbatim, while leaving the genuine risk warning unflagged.

20-minimal-banner.txt.scenario: A single-line banner: product + 'Capital at risk.'
20-minimal-banner.txt.why: Format-appropriateness: an honest minimal banner with a risk line must PASS — don't demand a fee schedule a banner can't carry, and don't flag the risk line.

21-negation-redflags.txt.scenario: Compliant copy stuffed with red-flag PHRASES used in negation.
21-negation-redflags.txt.why: The hardest false-positive test: every phrase a red-flag matcher keys on appears here — all in anti-hype framing. NONE may be flagged; the judge must read intent and PASS it.

22-complex-autocall-simple.txt.scenario: A complex structured product sold to retail as 'simple, smart investing'.
22-complex-autocall-simple.txt.why: An autocall note with unexplained coupon/barrier mechanics branded 'simple' and better than cash — misleading simplicity claim about a complex, capital-at-risk product.

23-past-performance-figure.txt.scenario: Past-performance figure WITH the standard disclaimer and a risk warning.
forbid_flag: Past performance is not a reliable indicator
23-past-performance-figure.txt.why: Framing is careful (disclaimer + risk warning present), so no breach — but the specific figure is an external fact → needs_review. The disclaimer must not be flagged. Tests the compliant-vs-needs_review boundary.

24-educational-what-is-etf.txt.scenario: Neutral educational explainer with an explicit 'not a recommendation' note. No promotion.
24-educational-what-is-etf.txt.why: Genuine educational content that correctly disclaims itself as non-advice — nothing to flag. Tests that the judge does not manufacture breaches from neutral, self-aware information.
